report.headline: Usage projected to rise toward the EuroLeague average, but the accompanying efficiency projection carries no real information

projection.text: Projected usage rate in the EuroLeague is 23.1%, up from 17.6% in the 2015-16 NBA season and roughly at the EuroLeague's minutes-weighted average of 20.0%.

risks.text: The true shooting projection of 56.5% should not be trusted: its out-of-fold error (4.7%) is no better than the trivial league-mean baseline (4.7%), meaning it carries no more information than simply guessing the EuroLeague average.
Turnover rate was elevated in the source season at 21.0%, a risk if the projected rise in usage materializes.

The 115-transition sample underlying this estimate is drawn from movers who sat only -0.31 SD relative to their own league on average before moving, a modest selection margin that limits how much confidence to place in the fitted relationship.

Source-season true shooting was 51.5%, itself -0.53 SD below the NBA average, so any efficiency projection is being extrapolated from a below-average starting point using a model that does not outperform a naive baseline.

strengths.text: Usage rate is projected to climb from 17.6% (-0.50 SD in the NBA) to 23.1%, near the EuroLeague average of 20.0%, consistent with the typical role increase seen when NBA players move to the EuroLeague.
The usage-rate model has an out-of-fold error of 3.3% and beats the best trivial baseline (4.3%), so its usage projection is informative rather than noise.
In the source season the subject produced 7.033 assists per 75 possessions with a 28.7% assist rate, indicating a substantial playmaking role.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage spans 18.6% to 27.6%, a nine-point band equal to roughly two standard deviations of EuroLeague usage (SD 4.5%), so the model can rank this player against peers but cannot price an individual figure.
